channel.title: Sports Law and Governance Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Sports Law and Governance Journal (slgj.scholasticahq.com)

item.title: Foreword to SLGJ Special Edition, Safe Sport Commentaries | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Matthew Raj. This special edition brings together dynamic scholars from across the globe to explore innovative, cross-disciplinary approaches for safeguarding sport environments and advancing integrity through rigorous, forward-looking commentary.

item.title: Legal Vulnerabilities and Criminal Proceedings in Contact Sport: Ice Hockey and the Death of Adam Johnson | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Annette Greenhow, Matthew Raj. Adam Johnson’s death during a UK ice hockey game prompted a manslaughter investigation and major rule changes, highlighting the legal complexities and governance duties surrounding player safety in contact sports.

item.title: Athlete Vulnerabilities in Elite Sport Corruption: A Socio-Legal Commentary on Contemporary Developments within the European Sphere | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Christopher Hamerton. Corruption in sport, from ancient bribery to modern match-fixing and sextortion, is under intense scrutiny as Europe and the UK develop legal frameworks to safeguard integrity amid global financialisation.

item.title: Esports Governance and Safeguarding in Australia | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By James Birt. Australia can strengthen youth safety and competitive integrity in esports by integrating tournaments and platforms into national frameworks, including Sport Integrity Australia and the eSafety Commissioner, ensuring consistent safeguards nationwide.

item.title: Striking a Balance: Volunteers and Safe Sport | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Millie Jones. This commentary examines Queensland’s Blue Card scheme and volunteer liability in sport, highlighting the need for qualified engagement strategies to boost volunteer participation while minimising harm risk.

item.title: Playing the game: The Organisation of Participant Safety in UK Sport - A Legal Commentary | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Christopher Hamerton, Matthew Raj. This commentary explores how UK law navigates the tension between autonomy, risk, and safety in sport, offering a comparative lens to Australia and highlighting recent safeguarding reforms.

item.title: Beyond the Playing Field: Rethinking Sport Safety in the Australian Defence Force | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Robin Orr. Sport is central to ADF culture yet presents an injury burden. Civilian injury prevention models fall short. The ADF needs bespoke strategies to safeguard readiness without losing sport’s vital benefits.

item.title: Making Headway on Sports Concussion: Sport-Specific Strategies for Concussion Prevention | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Marcus Moore. One sport-specific change—strategically chosen to dramatically reduce concussions while preserving the essence and appeal of the game—could boost sport safety in soccer, football, basketball and hockey.

item.title: Governance on Thin Ice: Evaluating Transparency and Accountability in the Brendan Kerry Case | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Jay W Merchant. Calls on SafeSport to publish redacted findings in Brendan Kerry’s case to restore transparency, protect athletes, and strengthen accountability after seven years and his 2024 permanent U.S. figure skating ineligibility.

item.title: Semenya v. Switzerland [GC]: Grand Chamber Judgment Expands Swiss Federal Tribunal’s Role in Protecting Human Rights in Sports | Published in Sports Law and Governance Journal
item.description: By Dr Tsubasa Shinohara. The Semenya judgment marks a turning point in sports and human rights, strengthening judicial review of Swiss Federal Tribunal (SFT) and reinforcing effective protection of fundamental rights under the ECHR.
